source: npm pack @modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres@0.6.2; read dist/index.js (single compiled file)

query.rationale: Runs arbitrary SELECT against the user's Postgres DB (credentials in CLI connection string, may be localhost/intranet) and returns rows; wrapped in a Postgres READ ONLY transaction so it cannot write, hence no SINK.

notes: Single tool 'query'; no CLI flags, env toggles, or read/write modes exist. Connection string (incl. credentials + host) is argv[0]; DB reached with the user's own credentials => SECRET regardless of target.

Every call is wrapped in 'BEGIN TRANSACTION READ ONLY' ... 'ROLLBACK' (index.js:90,102), so no write/DDL and no attacker-readable delivery => not SINK. A read-only tx still executes attacker-injectable SQL-in-context but produces no outbound channel by itself.
Also exposes MCP resources (table schemas) but the input snapshot lists only the 'query' tool.
Primary threat model: rows in the user's own DB are not attacker-controlled, so no UNTRUSTED at default; secondary variant treats stored rows as UNTRUSTED (end users/collaborators write them).
